title: Adding up with a condition: SUMIF
summary: Add up the sales that meet one condition, with the condition written in the formula or in a cell.
intro:
`SUMIF` adds up the values that meet one condition. It takes three arguments: the range where the condition is checked, the condition itself, and the range of values to add.

You can write the condition as text between quotation marks, such as `"North"`, or make it a reference to a cell, so the result changes when that cell changes.

faq.q: In what order do the arguments of `SUMIF` go?
faq.a: The condition range, then the condition, then the range to add: `=SUMIF(B2:B7,"North",C2:C7)`.

faq.q: Does letter case matter in the condition?
faq.a: No, matching in conditions does not tell upper case from lower case.

sumif-worked-example.prompt: `SUMIF` adds up the values that meet a condition. In `F2`, type the formula `=SUMIF(B2:B7,"North",C2:C7)` to add up the sales of the North region.
sumif-worked-example.explain: The condition is checked in `B2:B7`, and the matching values are added from `C2:C7`.

sumif-south.prompt: In `F3`, write a formula that adds up the sales of the South region.

criterion-in-a-cell.prompt: Instead of typing the region name inside the formula, the condition can be a reference to a cell. In `F2`, type the formula `=SUMIF(B2:B7,E2,C2:C7)`.

criterion-in-e4.prompt: In `F4`, write a formula that adds up the sales of the region written in `E4`.

sum-range-role.prompt: In `=SUMIF(B2:B7,"North",C2:C7)`, what is the role of `C2:C7`?
options: The range where the condition is checked
The range whose values are added

missing-quotes.prompt: What happens if you type the word North in the formula without quotation marks?
options: The formula works as it is
It adds up all the sales
